meta.title: Daily Reflection Tree
meta.author: Vaishnavi Dhage
meta.description: A deterministic decision tree to guide employees through daily self-reflection across three psychological axes: Agency, Contribution, and Concern.

axes.axis_1: Agency — Did I have control over my day?
axes.axis_3: Concern — Did I care for myself and others?

tree.question: How are you feeling as the day ends?
tree.subtext: Be honest with yourself. No right or wrong answer here.

next.question: Did you make progress on something that matters to you?
next.subtext: Even small wins count — finishing a task, learning something, having a good conversation.

next.question: Did you do something that pushed you slightly outside your comfort zone?
next.subtext: Growth often hides in small uncomfortable moments.

next.title: You're in a growth phase
next.message: Progress + discomfort = growth. You did both today.
next.insight: Tomorrow: Write down one thing you learned today before you sleep.

next.title: Solid, grounded day
next.message: Not every day needs to be a breakthrough. You made progress and that's genuinely good.
next.insight: Tomorrow: Pick one thing that would make tomorrow feel like a good day too.

options.label: Not really, but I feel okay

next.question: Did you take care of yourself today — rest, food, water, movement?

options.label: Yes, I took care of myself

next.title: You took care of yourself
next.message: Rest is not laziness. Recovery is part of the process.
next.insight: Tomorrow: You're recharged. What's one small step on something you've been postponing?

options.label: Not really, I need to do better

next.title: Your body is waiting for you
next.message: The basics — water, sleep, food, movement — keep everything else working.
next.insight: Tonight: Drink a glass of water right now. Sleep before midnight.

next.question: What felt heavier today — your tasks or your emotions?
next.subtext: Sometimes the day is hard because of work. Sometimes it's just how we feel inside.

next.question: Did you at least finish the most important thing on your list?
next.subtext: One done task beats ten half-done ones.

options.label: Yes, the key thing is done

next.title: The important thing got done
next.message: Even when the day felt scattered, you finished what mattered. That's real discipline.
next.insight: Tomorrow: Start with your #1 priority before anything else.

options.label: No, I got stuck or distracted

next.question: Do you know why you got stuck?
next.subtext: Awareness is the first step to fixing it.

next.title: Awareness is already progress
next.message: You know what blocked you. That awareness means tomorrow can be different.
next.insight: Tonight: Write down the blocker and one tiny thing you could do differently tomorrow.

options.label: Not sure, it just didn't happen

next.title: Time to get curious, not critical
next.message: You got stuck but you're not sure why. Don't beat yourself up — get curious instead.
next.insight: Try this: Think back to when you last felt productive. What was different?

options.label: My thoughts and emotions were heavy

next.question: Did you talk to someone about how you felt, or did you keep it to yourself?

next.title: Connection is healing
next.message: Sharing what you feel — even a little — is brave. You didn't carry it alone today.
next.insight: Notice: Did talking help? Even if just a little?

next.title: It's okay, but don't make it a habit
next.message: Sometimes we need quiet to process. But keeping everything inside too long makes it heavier.
next.insight: Tonight: Write 3 lines in a journal. What happened. How it felt. What you wish was different.

next.question: On days like this, what usually helps you reset?
next.subtext: Think about what has worked for you before.

next.title: Rest through what you love
next.message: On heavy days, creative outlets aren't escaping — they're resetting.
next.insight: Tonight: Do that thing. No guilt. It's part of recovery.

next.title: Move it out
next.message: Your body holds the stress your mind can't process. Movement is one of the fastest resets.
next.insight: Even a 10-minute walk outside can shift your mood. Try it tonight.

options.label: Sleep — tomorrow is a new day

next.title: Sleep is the real reset button
next.message: Sometimes the bravest thing is to close the day, let it go, and trust tomorrow will be different.
next.insight: Tonight: Put your phone down 20 mins before sleep.

next.question: I'm sorry it was hard. What made it difficult?
next.subtext: Naming it helps. You don't have to solve it, just see it.

next.question: Was the frustrating thing in your control — or outside it?
next.subtext: This matters. We often drain energy fighting things we can't change.

next.title: You can fix this — and you know it
next.message: The frustrating thing was in your hands. That means the solution is too.
next.insight: Tomorrow: Write one concrete action you can take. Specific. Small. Doable.

next.title: This one's not yours to carry
next.message: Spending energy on things outside your control drains you without changing anything.
next.insight: Ask yourself: Is there anything I can actually do about this? If no — let it go for tonight.

options.label: I felt anxious or low all day

next.question: Did the anxiety have a clear reason, or did it just show up?
next.subtext: Sometimes we know why. Sometimes it just comes.

next.title: You named it. That's power.
next.message: When anxiety has a name, it's no longer just a fog. You can work with something you can see.
next.insight: Tonight: Write the trigger. Then write: What's the worst realistic thing that could happen?

options.label: It just showed up, no clear reason

next.title: Sometimes anxiety just shows up
next.message: Not every bad feeling has a reason. That doesn't make it less real. It will pass.
next.insight: Try 4-7-8 breathing: Inhale 4 sec, hold 7, exhale 8. Do it 3 times.

options.label: I just couldn't get myself to do anything

next.question: Did you eat well and sleep okay last night?
next.subtext: Motivation is often just a physical state in disguise.

next.title: This might be burnout or disconnection
next.message: When basics are fine but you still can't move — that's a signal worth listening to.
next.insight: Ask: When did I last feel genuinely interested in something? Try a tiny bit of that this week.

next.title: Your foundation needs fixing first
next.message: Motivation, focus, mood — they all run on sleep, food, and water.
next.insight: Tonight: Sleep is your #1 job. Get 7-8 hours. Everything else can wait.
